steelman: Synchronous consumer-side calls are a first-order, textbook Kafka lag hypothesis: if one consumer performs a blocking external call (e.g., a database lookup) per message, throughput on that partition drops while all others remain healthy — precisely the single-partition lag pattern observed here. A determined defender could argue that the 'message processing time' metric reported in xbase captures only framework-level latency (e.g., the time between poll() returning and the offset commit), and may not include time spent inside the consume callback waiting on an external service; under that reading, the metric could be systematically undercounting the true wall-clock cost of processing. On that interpretation the consumer-side hypothesis would still be alive and would belong on a rigorous checklist item: 'verify wall-clock consumer thread time, not just poll-level metrics.' A senior Kafka engineer encountering this symptom blind would name synchronous lookups as a top-two candidate before any broker metric was examined.
mechanism_if_any: Consumer performs a synchronous external call (e.g., DB lookup) per message inside the consume loop, reducing per-message throughput for that partition's assigned consumer while others remain unaffected.
notes: The steelman (metric incompleteness) is the strongest available argument, but xbase closes it on two independent grounds: (1) 'message processing time matches the other partitions exactly' — if synchronous calls were inflating processing time it would show up in this comparison; (2) broker-2 is pegged at 95% disk I/O providing a complete, independent broker-side explanation. The closure is tight. No repair needed — the seed is clean on this lens.
